title: Ginkgolide B attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury via inhibition of ferroptosis through disrupting NCOA4-FTH1 interaction.
authors: Yang, Yuwei; Wu, Qing; Shan, Xin; Zhou, Haiyan; Wang, Jinwen; Hu, Yue; Chen, Jing; Lv, Zhiyang
one_liner_zh: 研究银杏内酯B通过干扰NCOA4-FTH1蛋白互作抑制铁死亡以减轻脑缺血再灌注损伤，虽涉及蛋白互作但非DNA体系，且方法以湿实验为主，仅分子对接辅助，与本课题TF-DNA互作建模无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major cause of neuronal damage and death. Ginkgolide B (GB) has been shown to exhibit neuroprotective effects in various brain injury models. AIM OF STUDY: The aim of study was to investigate the potential role of GB in protecting against cerebral I/R injury and explore the underlying mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) followed by reperfusion in order to trigger cerebral I/R injury. The rats were treated with different doses of GB, vehicle control or positive drug. Neurological function, infarct volume, and levels of ferroptosis markers were evaluated. In vitro experiments were performed using OGD/R-induced PC12 cells to further investigate the effects of GB on ferroptosis and its mechanisms. In addition, molecular docking, and microscale thermophoresis (MST) assay were conducted to explore the combination of GB and NCOA4. RESULTS: Reduced infarct volume and enhanced neurological function were signs of dose-dependent protection from cerebral I/R injury by GB therapy. Additionally, GB treatment had an impact on the levels of oxidative stress and ferroptosis markers, including reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and Fe(2+) in the cerebral environment during IR injury. Moreover, relevant ferroptosis key factors such as ACSL4, GPX4, FTH1, and NCOA4 can be regulated by GB. In OGD/R-induced PC12 cells, GB protected against ferroptosis by inhibiting autophagy and disrupting the interaction of NCOA4-FTH1. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that GB may protect against cerebral I/R injury by inhibiting ferroptosis through disrupting NCOA4-FTH1 interaction. GB has potential therapeutic applications for cerebral I/R injury, and further investigation of the underlying mechanisms and clinical trials are warranted.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：脑缺血/再灌注（I/R）损伤是神经元损伤和死亡的主要原因。银杏内酯B（GB）已在多种脑损伤模型中显示出神经保护作用。研究目的：本研究旨在探讨GB在保护脑I/R损伤中的潜在作用，并探索其潜在机制。材料与方法：成年雄性Sprague-Dawley大鼠暴露于短暂大脑中动脉闭塞（tMCAO）后恢复灌注，以诱发脑I/R损伤。大鼠分别接受不同剂量的GB、载体对照或阳性药物治疗。评估神经功能、梗死体积及铁死亡标志物水平。体外实验采用OGD/R诱导的PC12细胞，进一步研究GB对铁死亡的影响及其机制。此外，通过分子对接和微量热泳动（MST）实验探索GB与NCOA4的结合。结果：GB治疗对脑I/R损伤的保护作用表现为剂量依赖性，包括梗死体积减小和神经功能增强。此外，GB治疗影响I/R损伤期间脑环境中氧化应激和铁死亡标志物的水平，包括活性氧（ROS）、丙二醛（MDA）、超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）和Fe(2+)。同时，GB可调节相关铁死亡关键因子，如ACSL4、GPX4、FTH1和NCOA4。在OGD/R诱导的PC12细胞中，GB通过抑制自噬和破坏NCOA4-FTH1相互作用来保护细胞免受铁死亡。结论：我们的研究结果表明，GB可能通过破坏NCOA4-FTH1相互作用抑制铁死亡，从而保护脑I/R损伤。GB对脑I/R损伤具有潜在的治疗应用价值，进一步研究其潜在机制和临床试验是有必要的。
